en: Ferdinand Magellan did not discover the Philippines, as indigenous communities already thrived there long before his arrival in Homonhon in 1521.
Jose Rizal never served as president of the Philippines; Emilio Aguinaldo held that title as the first president of the First Philippine Republic.
The Philippine national flag was not designed by an American, but was conceptualized by Emilio Aguinaldo and sewn by Marcela Marino de Agoncillo.
Philippine Independence Day is not celebrated on the Fourth of July, but is officially observed every year on June 12.
The Filipino national language is not based on English, but is primarily rooted in Tagalog alongside other native Philippine languages.
The Philippine Legislative Branch does not execute laws, as it solely holds the power to create, amend, and repeal national legislation.
The Barong Tagalog is not made of thick fabric to hide weapons, but uses sheer pineapple fiber to prove the wearer carries no arms.
The Philippine Senate does not represent specific legislative districts, as its twenty-four members are elected nationally by the entire voting population.
National hero Jose Rizal did not lead an armed rebellion, but instead advocated for peaceful political reforms through his writings and organizations.
The Philippines does not have just one official language, as both Filipino and English are constitutionally designated as official languages.
The secret revolutionary society Katipunan was not founded by Jose Rizal, but was established by Andres Bonifacio in 1892.
Fe del Mundo was not a male student, but made history as the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936.
